goal: Give the csv_ingest advisory-lock key, the contact_csv_uploads terminal write, the Solicitation batch gate re-check, and the settings-owner route preamble exactly one owner each, and decompose the fallow complexity hotspots in the contacts ingest lane and the Solicitation batch executor until no fallow complexity suppression remains — with zero change to observable behavior.
non_goals: No behavior change of any kind: same statuses, same reports, same withhold reasons, same HTTP status codes, same log lines.
No schema change and no migration (head stays 089).
No new feature flag and no new env var.
No change to restraint-policy decisions, the Batch candidate window query semantics, or Ask evidence shape.
recordCompletedChildRuns is deliberately NOT decomposed (two set-based INSERTs each followed by a count assertion; splitting adds names without hiding complexity). Verdict logged on #565.
No change to the failed-hook outbox CAS choreography or crash-net bookkeeping — those stay in worker/jobs/*/failed-hook.ts.
Not touching worker/jobs/zernio/ingest-failed-hook.ts (the mirrored terminalizer) — a separate lane, separate table.
user_visible_behavior: None. This is a behavior-preserving refactor; the acceptance test is that every existing unit + integration suite stays green unmodified except where a call signature moved.
invariants: Invariant #15: src/lib/** and worker helpers receive their DB client explicitly — the extracted requireSettingsOwner takes (sql, request); route-helpers.ts must NOT import @/lib/db/server.
Invariant #2: the transactional outbox coupling is untouched — every terminal write stays in the SAME transaction as its outbox CAS.
Invariant #8: every extracted query keeps its account_id/business_id scoping predicates verbatim.
Invariant #12: entry points orchestrate, modules own failure behavior — the uploads route delegates the business-ownership check into the module rather than growing a second branch.
csv_ingest concurrency contract: the per-business advisory lock is the FIRST statement of every transaction that writes contact_csv_uploads, and every writer uses the SAME key.
PII contract: the ingest lane and the batch executor never log names, emails, phones, notes, or raw CSV text — counts and closed enums only.

Terminal-write contract after this change: every contact_csv_uploads terminal write carries the status='pending' predicate. The ingest path already holds the lock and has verified pending, so the predicate is a no-op there and its 0-row result is an impossible state.
edge_cases: Ingest path terminal write matching 0 rows: impossible under the held lock — must throw with context, not silently continue (previously unrepresentable because the UPDATE was unguarded).

failed-hook and terminalizeUploadForInactiveSubscription terminal write matching 0 rows: legitimate no-op (lost race against a concurrent terminal write / completed job) — must stay silent, so the shared writer returns a boolean rather than throwing.

prepareBatch and constructBatch re-check the same gate (flag / subscription / offboarding) at two different times by design; sharing the check must NOT collapse them into one evaluation — construction's re-check is the load-bearing one.
The shared gate helper must preserve each caller's DIFFERENT failure posture: prepareBatch fails an activeParent only when one exists; constructBatch always fails preparation.parentRunId.
requireSettingsOwner rejects an ?accountId query parameter BEFORE resolving the owner — the order is the guard, not an optimization.
Extracting requireSettingsOwner must not change the auto-approval route's impersonation branch, which runs AFTER the shared preamble and only on PATCH.
fallow runs --gate new-only --base origin/main: moved code counts as new, so a decomposition that merely relocates a hotspot will still fail the gate.
existing_patterns_to_follow: src/lib/solicitation/ingest.ts parseIngestReportValue — the house comment style for a single-owner helper whose callers pick their own failure posture.

src/lib/auth/route-helpers.ts requireOwnerWithAccount / requireWritableOwner — the { ok: true, ... } | { ok: false, response } result shape and the describe(<fnName>) test style in src/lib/auth/__tests__/route-helpers.test.ts.
worker/jobs/csv-ingest/__tests__/index.test.ts:169 — the raw-SQL-text assertion style that pins the advisory-lock key.
src/lib/solicitation/batch-builder.ts closedGateReason — the existing pure gate-reason function the shared gate helper wraps.
src/lib/solicitation/uploads.ts createContactsCsvUpload — the existing { ok: false, error } result union the business-ownership check joins.

the csv-ingest failed hook takes the advisory lock through acquireCsvIngestLock

writeTerminalUploadState returns false when no pending row transitioned

estimated_diff_size: ±600 lines across ~17 files; production lines near net-zero or negative (decomposition + de-duplication), growth is tests
rollback_plan: No schema change, no migration, no flag. Rollback is a straight revert of the squash-merge commit; nothing to un-apply on either Supabase project. The staging ride precedes the prod merge, so a defect surfaces before promotion.
observability: The '[csv-ingest] csv ingest completed' log line keeps its exact field set (upload_id, contacts_created, contacts_merged, visits_added, duplicate_visits, rejected_total, solicitation_batches_created, build_solicitation_batch_jobs_enqueued, rejected_* histogram) — a missing or renamed field means the refactor changed the ingest report path.

The '[SolicitationBatchWorker.failed] solicitation batch build exhausted' line keeps status/batch_id/business_id/outbox_attempt/error_class/parent_terminalized — proof the failed-hook decomposition preserved the terminal bookkeeping.
Sentry tags worker:'csv_ingest', kind:'on_failed_handler_crash' still fire from the crash-net path.

Staging smoke: one CSV upload lands status='completed' with a non-null report and raw_csv NULL, and its Solicitation batch reaches built_at non-null with the same send/withhold counts the pre-refactor run produced.
